what_its_for: Sutimlimab-jome is used to treat adults with cold agglutinin disease (CAD), a rare blood disorder where your immune system mistakenly destroys your own red blood cells, causing anemia (low red blood cell counts). This medicine helps stop the destruction of red blood cells so your body can maintain healthier blood counts and reduce symptoms like fatigue, shortness of breath, and yellowing of the skin or eyes.
how_to_take: Sutimlimab-jome is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into a vein by a healthcare professional in a clinic or infusion center. You will not inject this medicine yourself at home. Each infusion takes about 1 hour. You must receive certain vaccines before starting this medicine — talk to your doctor about required vaccinations at least 2 weeks before your first dose.
dosing: Your dose is based on your body weight. If you weigh less than 75 kg (about 165 pounds), the typical dose is 6,500 mg. If you weigh 75 kg or more, the typical dose is 7,500 mg. You will receive infusions on Day 0, Day 7, and then every 2 weeks after that. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given to you by a healthcare provider, it is important to keep all of your scheduled appointments. If you miss or need to reschedule an infusion, contact your doctor or infusion center as soon as possible. Do not try to make up a missed dose on your own — your healthcare team will help you get back on the right schedule.
storage: Sutimlimab-jome is stored and handled by the healthcare facility where you receive your infusions. You do not need to store this medicine at home. If you have any questions about storage, ask your pharmacist or healthcare provider.
what_to_avoid: Avoid receiving live vaccines (such as the MMR, chickenpox, or nasal flu vaccine) while on this medicine without first talking to your doctor, as it may raise your risk of infection. Tell all your doctors and dentists that you are taking this medicine before any procedures. Avoid close contact with people who are sick, and wash your hands frequently to help prevent infections.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency care right away if you experience: signs of a serious infection such as fever, chills, severe sore throat, or painful urination; signs of a severe allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, trouble breathing, or severe rash; unusual bruising or bleeding; dark or tea-colored urine; sudden worsening of tiredness or weakness; chest pain; or any new or concerning symptoms. This medicine can increase your risk of certain serious infections, especially meningococcal infection, which can be life-threatening.
when_it_works: Some patients begin to notice improvement in their symptoms and energy levels within the first few weeks of treatment as their red blood cell counts start to improve. However, it may take a few months to feel the full benefit. Your doctor will check your blood counts regularly to see how well the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: This medicine is only approved for use in adults. There is limited information about its use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, so talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you have kidney or liver problems, let your doctor know, as they will monitor you closely. Because this medicine affects your immune system, all patients must receive vaccinations against certain bacteria (especially meningococcus, pneumococcus, and Haemophilus influenzae type b) before starting treatment to help prevent serious infections.
